sections.heading: What it is and is not
sections.body:
- What it is: a first-party terminal coding agent that wires local tools, code, and workflows into a chosen LLM (`claim-crush-sf-identity`, `claim-crush-sf-what-it-is`)
- What it is not: a first-party desktop IDE or web editor (`claim-crush-sf-what-it-is-not`). It is not a managed-cloud agent host on opened product pages (`claim-crush-sf-not-for-product`)

sections.heading: Architecture and agent-loop ownership
sections.body:
- Primary type: `runtime` (`claim-crush-sf-primary-type`)
- Agent-loop owner: Crush (`claim-crush-sf-agent-loop`, `claim-crush-sf-agent-loop-readme`)
- Architecture: Go terminal UI on Bubble Tea, Bubbles, Lip Gloss, and Glamour (`claim-crush-sf-architecture`); crushrc Bash config, local state database, optional `crush serve` (`claim-crush-sf-architecture-readme`)

sections.heading: Surfaces and execution location
sections.body:
- Surface IDs: `surface-crush-cli`, `surface-crush-android-terminal`, `surface-crush-serve`, `surface-crush-ssh-generic`
- Execution location: same-device current working directory (`claim-crush-sf-execution-local`)

sections.heading: Model/auth/provider strategy
sections.body:
- Model strategy: official Charm Hyper, provider API keys, OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible custom endpoints, and local-provider discovery; mid-session model switch keeps context (`claim-crush-sf-model-strategy`)
- Auth strategy: provider keys or env vars, plus Hyper authenticate for the official path (`claim-crush-sf-auth-strategy`). `OPENCODE_API_KEY` reuses OpenCode Zen and Go (`claim-crush-sf-reuses-opencode`)
- Provider support: the README env-var table plus custom and local providers (`claim-crush-sf-provider-support`, `claim-crush-sf-local-models`). Default catalog comes from Catwalk (`claim-crush-sf-compatibility-catwalk`)

sections.heading: Context, memory, compaction, and session behavior
sections.body:
- Context behavior: LSPs, instruction files, extra context paths, `.gitignore`, and `.crushignore` (`claim-crush-sf-context`)
- Memory: `~/.config/crush/CRUSH.md` and `~/.config/AGENTS.md` plus a project init file; a separate conversation-memory product is unknown (`claim-crush-sf-memory`)
- Compaction: `option auto-summarize` (`claim-crush-sf-compaction`)
- Session behavior: multiple per-project sessions, session picker, mid-session model switch (`claim-crush-sf-session`); quit continue hint on v0.89.0 (`claim-crush-sf-session-quit-hint`)

sections.heading: Tools, extensions, MCP, skills, hooks, and APIs
sections.body:
- Tools: bash, view, ls, grep, glob, edit, write, multiedit, agent, agentic_fetch, and `mcp_*` (`claim-crush-sf-tools`); sourcegraph as a deniable built-in on the README (`claim-crush-sf-tools-sourcegraph`)
- Extensions: MCP, skills, LSPs, and hooks; no first-party plugin store established (`claim-crush-sf-extensions`)
- MCP: client for stdio, http, and sse, with optional OAuth (`claim-crush-sf-mcp`)
- Skills: Agent Skills `SKILL.md` discovery, including a builtin crush-config skill (`claim-crush-sf-skills`)
- Hooks: preliminary; only `PreToolUse` is documented as shipping (`claim-crush-sf-hooks`)
- APIs: `crush serve` `POST /v1/workspaces` plus SSE (`claim-crush-sf-api`)

sections.heading: Orchestration and parallelism
sections.body:
- Orchestration: large/small model slots (`claim-crush-sf-orchestration`); sub-agent tools (`claim-crush-sf-orchestration-hooks`); `crush serve` workspaces (`claim-crush-sf-orchestration-serve`)
- Parallelism: multiple sessions and multi-client serve attach (`claim-crush-sf-parallelism`); hooks for one event run in parallel (`claim-crush-sf-parallelism-hooks`); agent teams unknown

sections.heading: Isolation, permissions, security, and data path
sections.body:
- Isolation: unknown (`claim-crush-sf-isolation`)

- Data path: opt-out usage metrics that exclude prompts; local `.crush` logs; Hyper official path claimed ZDR (`claim-crush-sf-data-path`, `claim-crush-sf-data-path-hyper`)

sections.heading: Unique edge, meaningful drawbacks, best fit, and not-for
sections.body:
- Unique edge: Charm-stack terminal runtime with crushrc, LSP context, MCP, mid-session model switch, and official Hyper (`claim-crush-sf-unique`)
- Meaningful drawbacks: FSL competing-use (`claim-crush-sf-lock-in`); optional Hyper billing (`claim-crush-sf-lock-in-hyper`); hooks limited to PreToolUse (`claim-crush-sf-drawback-hooks`); trusted project config (`claim-crush-sf-drawback-trusted-config`)

claims.claim: crush serve exposes POST /v1/workspaces plus a per-workspace SSE event stream; clients sharing a resolved --cwd join one workspace and share sessions, message history, the permission queue, LSP, and MCP state. The session picker surfaces IsBusy (agent turn in flight) and AttachedClients (viewer count). The first client to create a workspace fixes process-wide --yolo and --debug flags on a first-wins basis; later clients with mismatched flags are logged but do not change the running workspace. A workspace tears down when its last SSE stream disconnects, with a short grace window after POST /v1/workspaces before reaping.

claims.notes: Product-page absences are claim-crush-sf-not-for-product and claim-crush-sf-what-it-is-not.

claims.claim: The README presents Crush as a terminal TUI/CLI with optional same-cwd crush serve. It does not offer a first-party web editor, desktop IDE, or managed-cloud agent host.
claims.notes: Absence of those downloads is not proof they will never exist. FSL competing-use is claim-crush-sf-not-for.

claims.claim: Config docs expose model large and model small slots for the selected large and small models.
claims.notes: Sub-agent tools are claim-crush-sf-orchestration-hooks. crush serve workspaces are claim-crush-sf-orchestration-serve.

claims.claim: Hook docs name sub-agents including the agent task tool and agentic_fetch, whose inner tool calls skip PreToolUse.
claims.notes: Large and small model slots are claim-crush-sf-orchestration. crush serve workspaces are claim-crush-sf-orchestration-serve.

claims.claim: The README says crush serve groups clients into workspaces keyed by resolved --cwd so they share sessions, history, the permission queue, LSP, and MCP state.
claims.notes: Large and small model slots are claim-crush-sf-orchestration. Sub-agent tools are claim-crush-sf-orchestration-hooks. Re-verified by claim-crush-gf2-serve-api (gap-fill-02 2026-08-16).

claims.claim: Users can keep multiple sessions per project. crush serve can attach several clients to one workspace. Concurrent independent agent teams were not established.
claims.value: multi-session and multi-client; agent teams unknown
claims.notes: Do not treat this as a parallel-agents product claim. Hook fan-out is claim-crush-sf-parallelism-hooks.

claims.claim: Hook docs say hooks run in parallel for speed and compose results in config order.
claims.value: hooks for one event run in parallel
claims.notes: Multi-session and crush serve multi-client are claim-crush-sf-parallelism. Re-verified by claim-crush-gf2-hooks (gap-fill-02 2026-08-16).

claims.claim: Crush asks before tool calls by default. permissions allow skips prompts, permissions deny hides tools, and --yolo skips all permission prompts.
claims.value: prompt by default; allow, deny, or --yolo
claims.notes: PreToolUse hooks can also allow or deny before the prompt.

claims.claim: Crush is distributed as an installable binary and package. Optional Charm Hyper inference is billed separately and is described as subscription-based with a free tier.
claims.value: installable binary; Hyper optional and billed separately
claims.notes: This page does not publish a Crush seat price. Do not treat that absence as a free-to-install or no-subscription sentence. Hyper dollar prices are claim-crush-sf-pricing-hyper.

claims.claim: Hyper's public pricing on 2026-08-14 is Free $0 with 100 Hypercredits per month, Subscription $20 per month with 250 Hypercredits refreshing daily, and prepaid bundles at $5/100, $10/500, and $20/2000 that never expire. One Hypercredit is currently 5 cents.
claims.notes: Hyper is Charm inference, not a Crush seat plan.

claims.claim: Crush owns the model-tool loop, sessions, tools, permissions, and context in a local terminal runtime. That supports primary type runtime.
claims.notes: Matches the candidate proposed_primary_type. No opened page said Crush wraps another vendor CLI.

claims.claim: The README env-var table names Hyper, Anthropic, OpenAI, Vercel AI Gateway, Gemini, Z.ai, MiniMax, Synthetic, Hugging Face, Cerebras, OpenRouter, io.net, Alibaba Singapore and US, Groq, Avian, OpenCode Zen and Go, Vertex AI, Amazon Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, and Moonshot.
claims.notes: Custom providers can add others. This is not a frozen model catalog.

claims.claim: Documented remote routes are generic SSH to a Crush process and multi-client attachment to crush serve. A first-party vendor-relay remote-control product was not established.
The canonical public source repository is https://github.com/charmbracelet/crush.
claims.notes: Public, not archived, default branch main.

claims.claim: The README env-var table says OPENCODE_API_KEY authenticates OpenCode Zen and Go inside Crush.
claims.notes: Supports crush --reuses_auth_from--> opencode. This is subscription reuse, not wraps_cli. Re-verified by claim-crush-gf2-auth-opencode (gap-fill-02 2026-08-16).

claims.claim: crushrc and crush.json are trusted code. crushrc runs in a full shell and crush.json $(...) expansions run at load time. The README says not to launch Crush in a directory whose config you have not reviewed.
claims.value: trusted local config executed at startup

claims.claim: Crush is session-based: multiple work sessions and contexts per project, a session picker, and mid-session model switches that keep context.
claims.value: multiple per-project sessions with picker and mid-session model switch
claims.notes: The quit-splash continue hint is claim-crush-sf-session-quit-hint. crush serve clients start a fresh session by default and must pick an in-progress session to join it.

claims.claim: Release v0.89.0 says quitting Crush shows a splash screen with a hint on how to continue from the session you left.
claims.notes: Per-project sessions and the session picker are claim-crush-sf-session.

claims.claim: Crush implements the Agent Skills standard via SKILL.md packages from global and project paths, including .agents/skills, .crush/skills, .claude/skills, and .cursor/skills. Skills may be user-invocable from the command palette.
claims.notes: A builtin crush-config skill can change Crush settings. Re-verified by claim-crush-gf2-skills (gap-fill-02 2026-08-16).

claims.claim: Crush is an actively shipped public product with a current GitHub latest release and install paths via Homebrew, npm, winget, Scoop, Charm apt/yum, Nix, FreeBSD pkg, and go install.
The README claims first-class support in every terminal on Android, alongside macOS, Linux, Windows, and BSD variants.
claims.notes: The opened README names Android, not a specific emulator. Supports surface-crush-android-terminal.

claims.claim: The primary surface is a first-party terminal TUI/CLI named crush, with commands such as crush logs, crush update-providers, and crush serve.
claims.notes: Supports surface-crush-cli. crush init is claim-crush-sf-surface-cli-init on the config docs.

claims.claim: Config docs name crush init as the command that creates the initialize-as context filename.
claims.notes: README crush logs, crush update-providers, and crush serve are claim-crush-sf-surface-cli.

claims.claim: crush serve is a first-party shared backend. Clients with the same --cwd join one workspace, share sessions, history, the permission queue, LSP, and MCP, and attach over POST /v1/workspaces plus an SSE event stream.
claims.notes: Supports surface-crush-serve. Bind address and auth were not specified on the opened README section. Re-verified by claim-crush-gf2-serve-api (gap-fill-02 2026-08-16).

claims.claim: Desktop-notification docs treat SSH as an expected way to reach a Crush process: auto uses native notifications locally and OSC notifications over SSH when supported. That is generic remote-shell reachability, not a first-party remoting product.
claims.value: generic SSH reachability with OSC notifications
claims.notes: Supports surface-crush-ssh-generic.

surfaces.notes: README first-class Android terminal claim. Opened pages do not name Termux or a native Android app. Distinct from iOS, which remains unknown.
Primary crush binary. Local start and local session resume. inspect_tools is unknown: opened pages do not state a tool-inspection UI. Not a desktop app or web editor.
Shared backend for TUI clients with the same --cwd. POST /v1/workspaces and SSE. Bind, auth, and remote-host deployment were not specified on the opened README section.
Notification docs treat SSH as expected reachability and switch to OSC there. This is not a first-party remoting UX or vendor relay.
